strengths: Strong empirical results on target datasets (BioVid: 81.5/78.0, StressID: 80.8/77.9 in WAR/F1), particularly notable gains in F1 indicating better class-imbalance handling
Thorough experimental evaluation with comprehensive baselines (6 CLIP-based FER + 6 TTA methods), extensive ablations, subject-wise results, and robustness testing across random seeds
Interpretable AU-based approach with qualitative validation showing predicted AU patterns align with external detector (OpenFace), valuable for clinical deployment
Well-motivated problem addressing subject-specific personalization for subtle expressions in healthcare applications, with clear presentation and informative figures
Computational efficiency demonstrated (lower parameters and GFLOPs than competitors while achieving better accuracy)
Practical approach avoiding costly AU annotations or LLM-generated prompts through structured AU prompting
weaknesses: Limited novelty: individual components are standard techniques (AU prompts replacing class prompts, lightweight MLP adapter, entropy minimization from TPT/TENT, simple 1D-CNN+GLU). Main contribution is primarily combinatorial rather than introducing novel concepts
Overstated claims about 'without AU supervision'—the method relies on hand-crafted FACS AU prompts encoding significant domain knowledge; better framed as 'without explicit AU annotations'

Poor generalization beyond pain/stress: BAH results show only +0.4% F1 improvement (41.1% vs 40.7%), suggesting method struggles with ambiguous expressions; FERV39K results notably weaker (47.3% WAR vs 78.0% on BioVid)

Impractical test-time adaptation requirements: requires per-subject video at test time with parameters reset per subject, limiting real-world deployment. Only 10 TTA iterations justified without justification

Limited theoretical justification for why AU prompting and entropy-guided TTA should improve fine-grained recognition; missing explanation for why entropy minimization is the right adaptation objective

Insufficient AU prediction analysis: Figure 4 qualitative only; no quantitative accuracy measurements against ground truth; unclear whether improvements stem from AU alignment or test-time adaptation per se
Baseline comparison fairness concerns: most baselines (TPT, TDA, etc.) designed for image classification; only one video baseline (T3AL); setup consistency unclear
Small target subject sets (10 per dataset) without statistical significance testing or confidence intervals; no cross-dataset evaluation or domain-shift analysis; only CLIP-ViT-B/32 evaluated
